chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Barqi, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his fathers, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said:
"Whoever eats something of the foul-smelling things, let him not approach the mosque."

key_terms.الْمُؤْذِيَاتِ: Foul-smelling things (specifically referring to foods like garlic and onions)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on entering the mosque after eating garlic or onions?
ai.summary: This narration from the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the concept of *ghabrat al-tha'ib* (odor of food) as a factor affecting mosque etiquette, extending the prohibition beyond physical impurity (*najāsah*) to sensory comfort. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on preserving the sanctity and communal harmony of the mosque, where even minor distractions like strong odors are discouraged to maintain reverence. This ruling is often discussed in the context of *adab al-masjid* (mosque etiquette) alongside physical cleanliness.
